new_statements.quote: Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345:] L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.
new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them currently shows any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length. The hypothesis will be raised again in diachrony, in the interpretation of the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345:] The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not force this solution for proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis is conceivable at an earlier stage of the evolution.
new_statements.citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale. Paris: Peeters (SELAF 357).
new_statements.locator: p. 285, 'Récapitulation contrastive', Remarque 2 (cross-referenced to p. 345, Remarque)

new_statements.rule_in_words: The Gbaya varieties covered by the old [mdo] code ('Buli, 'Biyanda, Toongo = Southwest Gbaya [gso]; Mbodomo = Gbaya-Mbodomo [gmm]) are two-tone (H/L) languages with no word-level accent: Moñino states explicitly that none of the 21 Gbaya-Manza-Ngbaka languages he surveyed shows any accent, intensity or length phenomenon. The primary Mbodomo grammar (Boyd 1997, sec. 2.4, p. 41) describes lexical and grammatical tone only and never mentions stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Moñino only entertains an accent as a possible pre-proto-Gbaya stage (p. 345), not in any modern language.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is made for the word/tone-melody level across the whole Gbaya group in a comparative work; the table on p. 285 in which it sits groups 'buli, 'biyanda and mbodomo (area a4) by their tonal behaviour in word sequences. Boyd 1997 (Mbodomo) is the only modern primary description and is silent on stress; its tone statement (p. 41) concerns words in isolation and in the clause.
new_statements.identity_note: sout3222 is not a language: it is Glottolog's bookkeeping placeholder for the retired ISO code [mdo] 'Gbaya, Southwest', split on 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-187, SIL Cameroon) into Southwest Gbaya [gso] = Glottolog sout2785 (CAR: 'Biyanda, 'Buli, Toongo etc.) and Gbaya-Mbodomo [gmm] = Glottolog gbay1281 (East Cameroon). The statement quoted (Moñino 1995 p. 285) covers exactly these varieties ('buli, 'biyanda, toongo, mbodomo are among his 21 languages, cf. informants p. 51-52); the primary grammar under the old code (Boyd 1997, WALS 'Mbodomo' mdo) describes Mbodomo of Cameroon only. Any catalog entry belongs under sout2785 and/or gbay1281, not under the retired code.

sources.locator: p. 285, 'Récapitulation contrastive', Remarque 2 (cross-referenced to p. 345, Remarque)
sources.note: p. 285, Remarque 2 (in the contrastive recapitulation of tone behaviour): none of the 21 languages surveyed shows any accent, intensity or length phenomenon; p. 345 Remarque: 'L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution [an accent in proto-Gbaya]'. The table on p. 285 places 'buli, 'biy[anda] and mbo[domo] together in tonal area a4.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 1997. A Phonology and Grammar of Mbódɔ́mɔ́. MA thesis, University of Texas at Arlington. 236 pp. (the primary phonology/grammar of the Cameroonian half of old [mdo]; WALS 'Mbodomo' code mdo cites it)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent (0 occurrences of 'stress' in the decoded text). Ch. 2 Phonology, sec. 2.4 Tone, p. 41: 'Mbódɔ́mɔ́ has both lexical tone and grammatical tone. Lexical tone is predominately a feature of nouns and modifiers.. Verbs, unlike nouns and modifiers, do not have tone as a contrastive feature. All verbs in isolation have the same tone pattern, high-low.' Sec. 2.4.1: two lexical tones, high and low; limited contour tones; sec. 2.3.1: the vowel is the tone-bearing unit.
